merge.title: MP-revision physical-access spec (buried/shielded display nets, no S-world test pads, no void behind the panel, destructive-open shell, published comparables) plus an optional passive PC13 case/display-removal input; active mesh dropped
merge.threat: An interdictor or evil maid opens the unit and solders an implant (MCU + radio) onto the write-only display bus (pq1: SPI1 PA4/PA5/PA7, DC PB0) or the button nets (PA0/PA1). The seed wizard paints the 24 words as pixels over SPI1 (secure/src/ui/seed_wizard.rs:89-96), and the panel has no MISO (secure/src/hw/lcd_nv3007.rs:104; fsbl/src/render.rs:62-72), so firmware cannot see a passive tap. Real-world shape: Joe Grand's Ledger Nano X implant (glyph template-matcher on the OLED SPI, LTE exfiltration). The proposals' name "CryptoBilis" appears in none of the sources. docs/security/user-device-verification.md:163-168 already records this as an accepted residual covered only by "packaging + photos + SE-CA check". Two windows: (1) factory to first power, with the device unpowered at RDP-0; (2) after ownership, with the device normally unplugged.
merge.proposal:
ONE recommendation in two tiers. Tier A carries the weight; Tier B is an optional cost-raiser.

TIER A — mechanical/PCB security spec for the MP revision of AL_A66_MB. Amend docs/hardware/hardware_requirements.md §Anti-tamper (rows :239-245 are all "board not started"); do not create a new doc.
1. Copper rule (the only near-deterministic part). Route SPI1 CS/SCK/MOSI, DC, RST and TE as stripline between two ground planes on the 6-layer stack, with no outer-layer vias in the display region. Plain "inner layer" is not enough: a capacitive pickup plate over an unshielded inner trace still recovers MOSI.
2. No test pads at MP on SPI1, I2C1 (PB8/PB9 are brought out on EVT, evt-debug-pins.md:45-46), I2C4, I2C2, PA0/PA1. This is already an unticked row (README.md:447, hardware_requirements.md:244).
3. Display stack: panel bonded to a rigid backer with no void behind it; display FPC captured under the EMI can; display and button connectors potted. State honestly that supercap/USB-C/dome-switch voids remain and button nets cannot be buried. A button tap leaks the PIN press pattern, not the seed, so rank SPI1/DC above the buttons.
4. Destructive-open shell (ultrasonic weld), claimed as evidence-of-opening and attacker cost, not prevention.
5. Golden comparables: publish Gerbers/netlist, a pinned BOM (exact passives), and reference photos, X-ray and weight of a sealed known-good unit. These are detection aids that depend on the user actually inspecting.
6. BOOT0: verify on MP silicon that the SBU -> R132 -> U111 -> R131 -> BOOT0 path is physically gone. Outside test: A8<->VBUS bridge must not enumerate 0483:df11. Plus one teardown.
7. A non-destructive pre-first-power SWD route must be part of the same spec. See decision_conflicts: invariant #10(a) and a welded shell are incompatible without it.

TIER B — passive external tamper on PC13 (TAMP_IN1). The pin is bonded and NC (pin 2); PC13 is VBAT-domain (RM0456 §10). Source: a normally-closed case-open switch in series with a continuity loop through the display FPC, with hardware pull + RC, using the FLTCR config already at tamp.rs:274-281. Firmware delta:
- Set TAMP1E and the CR2 trigger; add TAMP1F to the poll()/on_tamp_irq masks. Today they only test ITAMP_FLAG_MASK (tamp.rs:87, :372).
- Read TAMP_SR and escalate before the unconditional SCR clear (tamp.rs:272).
- At boot, sample the raw PC13 level before bhk::load_and_lock (main.rs:1529); an open loop goes to trigger_intrusion_wipe.
- Arm only in production; add a prodtest read (Trezor's `tamper-read` model).
- Select LSE as RTCCLK if a supercap exists (the crystal is on pins 5/6), which also makes ITAMP3 meaningful.

WHAT TIER B PLUS THE SHELL ACTUALLY BUY
- Transit (factory to first power): PC13 buys nothing. The unit is unpowered at RDP-0, nothing is armed, and firmware is not yet locked. The shell is the only control, and only if the user inspects it.
- Powered, post-ownership: an open leads to SRAM zeroize + page-125 wipe flag + reset, then SE factory reset at the next boot. Real but narrow: a signer is rarely attacked while plugged in.
- Unplugged within VBAT hold (about 12-24 h with a 0.47-1 F supercap, if one is populated at all): TAMP1F latches and is acted on at the next boot, provided the SCR-clear defect is fixed.
- Unplugged and drained (the normal resting state): only a loop that is still open at next boot is caught. An attacker who re-closes the switch or jumpers the two-wire loop is invisible. A passive input cannot detect shorts, and a fake panel or interposer simply carries the loop through.
- "Hardware erases the BHK" is not a durable response. BKP0R..7R are reloaded from the DHUK-wrapped page 126 every boot (bhk.rs:27-33). The only durable response is the software intrusion wipe.
Net: Tier B catches clumsy or powered opens. Tier A is the implant defence.

members.note: Passed all three round-1 lenses; it is the backbone (Tier A). Changes: (a) only the stripline/no-pad copper rule is close to deterministic; weld, photos, X-ray and weight are detection or cost claims; (b) 'inner layers' tightened to stripline between ground planes; (c) 'zero void' narrowed to the display stack; (d) 'CryptoBilis' name removed and the Parasitic Circus attribution corrected (that paper is PDN-impedance golden-free verification, not X-ray/weight); (e) schematic cross-check and BOM added as prerequisites; (f) BOOT0 folded into #695/#696 and BOM into #697; (g) SWD-route conflict with invariant #10 made explicit; (h) Trezor precedent added (Model One/T ultrasonic weld, Safe 3/5 tamper-evident casing).

Round-1 feasibility REFUTED (confidence 0.7); I re-checked the load-bearing points. (1) Pin plan wrong: on UFQFPN48 the only TAMP_OUT pads are PA0 (OUT1, LEFT KEY), PA1 (OUT4, RIGHT KEY) and PC13 (OUT2, same pad as IN1); PA10/PB4 carry no TAMP function (DS13086; pin table shows PA0/PA1 as the keys). An active pair needs a button moved. (2) 'CR3=0 erases the BHK in hardware' is not durable: bhk.rs:27-33 regenerates it from page 126 every boot. (3) No battery: the response is software at the next powered boot, pre-empted by waiting for drain and bridging OUT->IN at the QFN. (4) 'Read ATOR twice' is a register-read note, not an anti-glitch measure. Salvaged into Tier B: PC13 as a passive input, production-only arming, prodtest read, TRNG/TAMP prerequisites #47/#50/#75/#81/#391.

Passed feasibility (0.8) with re-scoping; kept as Tier B plus the seal/box-opening ceremony. Corrections applied: inherits the no-battery finding (software wipe at next boot only); BKPR erase is not the wipe; a two-wire flex loop is carried through by a fake panel or interposer, so the fake-screen residual is cost-raised, not closed; kind becomes mixed. One round-1 correction is itself WRONG and I overrule it: the D-08 feasibility verifier said LSI is outside the backup domain. RM0456 §10 says 'the VBAT pin powers the RTC and TAMP peripherals, the LSI and LSE oscillators' and 'LSE and LSI clocks are in the backup domain' (tamp.rs:238 uses RCC_BDCR.LSION). Filtered sampling therefore does run on VBAT, as the IMP-04 verifier said. Trezor precedent corrected: T3W1 has TAMP_IN2 hardware and driver, but shipped firmware disarms it.

dropped_parts: Active tamper mesh via ATCR1/ATCR2/ATSEEDR/ATOR (IMP-04): needs TAMP_OUT, which exists only on PA0/PA1 (the buttons) and PC13 itself, so a button must be re-routed; with no battery the comparator is dead whenever the unit is drained; an OUT->IN bridge at the package satisfies it permanently.
'TAMP_OUT on PA10/PB4' (IMP-04): false; those pads have no TAMP alternate function.

'A trip erases BKP0R..7R (BHK) in hardware' as the tamper response (IMP-04, D-08): the BHK is reloaded from DHUK-wrapped flash page 126 on every boot (bhk.rs:27-33; load at main.rs:1529). Only tzic::trigger_intrusion_wipe is durable.

'12-24 h armed when unplugged' as a coverage claim (IMP-04): depends on a supercap that hardware_requirements.md:245 marks 'board not started' and that user-device-verification.md:190-191 forbids; covers zero transit time.

4-layer LDS/PCB mesh over MCU + both SEs + display connector (IMP-04; also the existing hardware_requirements.md:106 row): as a passive loop into PC13 it detects only a still-open cut at next boot. Not worth mesh layers; the stripline + EMI can + potting of Tier A do the physical work. Recommend downgrading the existing row instead of leaving it as an unqualified requirement.
'The one measure that does not depend on detection thresholds' (IMP-01 rationale): true only for the copper/void rule.

'Open and compare' user inspection alongside a welded shell (D-08's Coldcard clear-case alternative as a co-equal option): mutually exclusive with destructive-open. Keep it as a documented, rejected alternative unless the owner picks it (see decision_conflicts).
Serialised tamper-evident seal as a security control (D-08): keep it as a ceremony item (README.md:459 row) but count it as deterrence only; adhesive seals are routinely defeated.

ADC sense resistor on the panel rail and GPIO RC/capacitance self-test of PA4/PA5/PA7 (round-1 complement to IMP-01): threshold-based, belongs to the display/implant-detection clusters. TSC fingerprinting of these nets is impossible anyway (AF9 only on PB4-7 and PB12-14).

Vendor precedents downgraded: Keystone 'PCI-level anti-tamper' is README marketing with no published mesh; Foundation 'factory reset on screen removal' is really 'tamper pins erase the Master Key' (audit-response wording, seen only as a search snippet); Trezor 'TAMP all-internal' is wrong (see precedent).
tracked_issues: #695 (open): sealed EVT flashable over the SBU bridge; BOOT0 strap at MP is an ODM statement. Covers Tier A item 6; add the MP silicon check.
#696 (open): with BOOT0 strapped + RDP-2, CMD_FW_* is the only field path. Coupled to removing the SBU->BOOT0 path.
#697 (open): confirm the production SE050 part with the ODM. Extend to the pinned full BOM.
#705 (open): FSBL cannot light the pq1 panel, so the boot fingerprint is dark on a sealed unit. The enclosure protects a trust anchor that is currently invisible.

#75 (open, ship-blocker): TAMP escalation log-only -> wipe, polled -> IRQ, IER audit. Hard prerequisite for Tier B. The issue body is partly stale: tamp-wipe already calls trigger_intrusion_wipe at tamp.rs:108.

#47 (open, ship-blocker): hardware-mode erase for BHK-protecting tampers. The base-address bug it names is fixed (tamp.rs:132); its 'do NOT erase page 126' item is exactly why BKPR erase is not a wipe.
#50 (open, ship-blocker) and #81 (open): TAMPSEC/TAMPPRIV/GTZC2. Without them NS can clear TAMP1E.
#391 (open): TAMP has never had a silicon test. Blocks arming any external input.

No issue exists for the enclosure, no-void display stack, display-net routing, test-pad removal, published comparables, external TAMP_IN1/PC13, or case switch. My searches for 'enclosure', 'tamper mesh', 'TAMP_IN', 'PC13', 'tamper-evident seal', 'TAMP_SCR' returned nothing; 'case switch' returned only unrelated hits.
merge.untracked_delta:
Six items have no issue.
1. One hardware issue for the MP physical-access spec (Tier A items 1-5 and 7), linked to #695/#696/#697/#705, amending hardware_requirements.md §Anti-tamper.
2. One issue for the external TAMP_IN1/PC13 passive input (Tier B), linked to #47/#50/#75/#81/#391/#256.
3. The TAMP_SCR clear-before-read and reset-race defect (see live_defects).
4. The owner decision on VBAT retention (supercap vs none); two recorded docs disagree.
5. The owner decision on where pre-first-power SWD lives on a welded MP unit.
6. Stale doc/comment lines:
   - hardware_requirements.md:101-102 says tamp is "not yet wired into main()"; main.rs:1400 and :4327 wire it.
   - main.rs:1395-1397 says "Log-only; never halts and never wipes"; false under tamp-wipe.
   - the hardware_requirements.md mesh row presents a mesh into TAMP_INx as sufficient without the no-battery caveat.
   - the task premise "no HSE" is firmware-only: the pin table shows an 8 MHz HSE and a 32 kHz LSE crystal fitted on pq1.
decision_conflicts: Invariant #10(a) vs destructive-open shell. #10 requires anyone to verify flash/option bytes/OTP over SWD before first power. Sealed EVT units have no exposed SWD (#695), and evt-debug-pins.md:161-162 keeps the SWD pads inside the shell. A welded shell makes the mandated verification destroy the tamper evidence. user-device-verification.md:184-189 already specifies the fix (SWDIO/SWCLK on USB-C SBU1/SBU2, inert after RDP-2; fallback pogo pads), but V10 uses SBU for the BOOT0 LDO path (evt-debug-pins.md:145-176). The MP board must swap SBU from BOOT0 to SWD, or expose sealed pogo pads, or the owner must re-scope #10(a). Owner decision required before the shell is specified.

VBAT retention. user-device-verification.md:190-191 requires 'No VBAT retention on the production board (no coin cell / supercap on the backup domain)' so that power removal clears volatile state. brownout-hardening.md:216-250, hardware_requirements.md:245 and #248 specify a 0.47-1 F VBAT supercap. They cannot both hold. If no-VBAT wins, Tier B is reduced to 'powered opens plus a loop still open at boot' and no unpowered latch exists at all.

Existing requirement rows vs the round-1 refutation. hardware_requirements.md:106-108/:239-240 and README.md:448 require a '4-layer tamper mesh into TAMP_INx' and a case switch. This is not an owner decision against the cluster, but the mesh row's implied value is refuted by the no-battery and reload-from-flash facts; recommend downgrading it rather than building it.

Open-inspection vs evidence-of-opening. No recorded owner decision either way (round-1 grep of CLAUDE.md/docs/memory, not re-run here). 'Published board photos for visual comparison' (user-device-verification.md:166) leans toward inspectability; a welded opaque shell removes it. Must be chosen deliberately.

No conflict with the recorded decisions I checked: ML-KEM descoping, keep-BHK-for-SE050, OPTIGA S-1/2/3 deferral, SHA-2. The cluster adds no FSBL bytes, no secure-slot bytes beyond a few register writes, and no runtime write to the FSBL range. Tier B's response path uses the existing page-125 wipe flag, so no new per-signature flash state.
hardware_asks: MP layout: SPI1 (PA4/PA5/PA7), DC PB0, RST PB1, TE PB2 as stripline between ground planes; no outer-layer vias in the display region; ODM to supply layer-by-layer evidence.

Shell: ultrasonic-welded or otherwise destructive-open; state the RMA consequence (no reopen).

Pre-first-power SWD without opening: move USB-C SBU1/SBU2 from the BOOT0 LDO (U111/R131/R132) to SWDIO/SWCLK with ESD protection, or provide externally reachable pogo pads. Coupled to the BOOT0 hard strap.
BOOT0: hard strap to GND and remove (not merely strap around) the SBU->U111->BOOT0 path; demonstrate on an MP unit that the A8<->VBUS bridge no longer enumerates 0483:df11.

Optional (Tier B): wire PC13 (pin 2, currently NC) to a normally-closed case-open switch in series with a continuity loop through the display FPC, with external pull + RC; keep the net short and inside the shielded/potted region. Do NOT move a button to free a TAMP_OUT pad.
Confirm whether V10 populates anything on VBAT (pin 1): supercap, tie to VDD, or other. The schematic PDF is not text-searchable and the repo does not say. Then implement the owner's VBAT decision.
Deliver netlist + BOM with exact passives; the repo has copper plots only (docs/hardware/pcb/README.md; schematics/README.md: 'There is no BOM in this repo').
Deliver reference photos, X-ray and weight of a sealed known-good MP unit for publication.

Owner decision: VBAT supercap vs no VBAT retention (decision_conflicts 2).

merge.precedent:
Enclosure (parity with every major vendor):
- Ledger Nano Gen5: casing that cannot be opened without visible, irreversible damage (support article 4404382029329). Ledger's stated response to the Nano X implant was "check hardware integrity against known-good pictures".
- Cypherock: ultrasonic weld; the Keylabs audit flagged exposed test points as a jig vector.
- Coldcard: welded clear case (coldcard.com/docs/physical-notes).
- Trezor: Model One/T ultrasonic weld; Safe 3/5 tamper-evident casing (trezor.io hardware-security page). Nothing in the trezor-firmware tree covers no-cavity, potting or test-pad removal.

External tamper input:
- Trezor T3W1 has a passive, level-mode TAMP_IN2 on PA0 in the driver (core/embed/sec/tamper/stm32u5/tamper.c:157-160, :196-207; TAMPER_INPUT_2 in boards/trezor_t3w1_rev{A,B,C}.h) and a prodtest `tamper-read`.
- The shipped path disarms it: core/embed/projects/secmon/main.c:113-114 calls tamper_init(); tamper_external_disable(); (re-read at HEAD 6ab39e95).
- The kernel's `#if PRODUCTION tamper_external_enable()` (kernel/main.c:139-143) sits under SECURE_MODE; T3W1's model.toml sets secmon = true and lists no secure_mode feature (the #ifdef at kernel/main.c:130 and the model.toml grep are my reads; the nesting itself is round-1's).
- Trezor has no ATCR/active-tamper code anywhere.
- Foundation Passport Prime: tamper pins under the display that erase the Master Key (vendor statement).
- GridPlus Lattice1: active LDS mesh, but with a roughly 5-year battery, which pq1 has excluded.
merge.rationale:
Why P1 overall, with a split inside it:
- Tier A spec, cross-check/BOM and the SWD-route decision are effectively P0-for-the-respin. The work is cheap now and impossible after MP tooling. It is the only control on the seed-over-SPI implant class, which firmware cannot detect because the panel is write-only.
- Tier B (PC13) is P2-P3. It is a narrow cost-raiser gated on four open TAMP ship-blockers and on a TAMP stack that has never run on silicon. Round-1 rated D-08 P2 and refuted IMP-04's P1.
- The SCR-clear/reset-race defect is independent of this cluster's hardware and should be fixed with #75 regardless.

Kind is mixed: hardware/ODM dominates; firmware is roughly tens of lines in tamp.rs plus a boot check. Cost L is driven by the board spin, ODM mechanical work and one destructive teardown.

Not re-verified by me (taken from round-1): DS13086 pin-function rows, the vendor web sources, and the Trezor git history of the external-tamper enable/disable. I did re-read the Trezor files at HEAD, the pq1 pin table, RM0456 §10 text, tamp.rs, bhk.rs, the main.rs ordering and the issues listed.

live_defects.what: tamp::init discards latched tamper flags before anything reads them, and the tamper response can be pre-empted by a reset. init_tamp_registers writes TAMP_SCR = 0x0007_FFFF (clears TAMP1F..8F and ITAMP1F/2F/3F) unconditionally at boot. Escalation happens only in poll() from SysTick (about 1 ms) or the IRQ handler. If ITAMP1 (backup-domain voltage), ITAMP2 (temperature) or ITAMP3 latches and the core resets before the next poll (a voltage glitch that also trips BOR, NRST, or power removal while VBAT holds), the next boot clears the flag, reloads the BHK from page 126 and continues with no wipe. ITAMP5..13 flags (bits 20-28) are outside the clear mask and would survive to the first poll. This is a desk finding from reading code, not reproduced; TAMP has never run on silicon (#391).
live_defects.evidence: secure/src/hw/tamp.rs:270-272 (comment 'Clear any pending tamper flags from a prior power cycle'); the only TAMP_SR reads are tamp.rs:86 (poll) and :372 (IRQ); main.rs:1400 (init) precedes main.rs:1529 (bhk::load_and_lock); bhk.rs:27-33 (BHK regenerated from flash each boot); Makefile:2662 RELEASE_FEATURES has tamp,tamp-wipe but not tamp-irq. Trezor has the same clear-at-init (tamper.c:118-121) but does not reload its key from flash.
live_defects.reachable_in_production_config: Plausible. The shipping feature set (tamp + tamp-wipe, polled) contains the path. The production image cannot be built today (S-2 fence), and whether flags latch across the reset depends on the VBAT wiring, which is unconfirmed on V10.
live_defects.severity: medium (FI-assisted, about 1 ms race; it defeats the wipe response for voltage/temperature tampers, not a direct key leak). Untracked.

live_defects.what: The external tamper input is inert end to end: no TAMPxE bit is ever set, and both handlers test only ITAMP_FLAG_MASK. A future hardware-only wiring of PC13 would do nothing.
live_defects.evidence: secure/src/hw/tamp.rs:274-281 ('We don't enable external pins here'), :87, :211-221, :372; pure_tests.rs:1728 negative_tamp_init_skips_external_pins (cited by round-1).
live_defects.reachable_in_production_config: Yes, by design; this is a gap, not a bug.

live_defects.what: Stale claims next to the code: hardware_requirements.md:101-102 says tamp is 'not yet wired into main()' and that the BHK 'is erased in hardware on any tamper event' (true only for the runtime copy); main.rs:1395-1397 says 'Log-only; never halts and never wipes', false under tamp-wipe.

merge.residual_after:
- Factory-inserted implant: one sealed inside the shell before welding is untouched. That is the job of the SWD-verify and birth-certificate clusters, and SWD verification proves firmware, not the board.
- Whole-device substitution or re-shelling: a counterfeit or re-welded shell defeats evidence-of-opening unless the user actually compares against the published photos, weight and X-ray.
- Transit: PC13 contributes nothing. A drained unit can be opened, implanted and the loop re-closed or jumpered with no trace in firmware.
- Fake panel or interposer: it carries the two-wire continuity loop through, so the accepted "later fake screen" residual stays, at higher cost.
- Non-contact capture: near-field EM pickup of the FPC/panel edge or the panel's own driver IC, optical capture of the screen, and button-contact probing all remain. Button nets terminate at mechanical contacts and cannot be buried.
- Pre-RDP-2 reflash: an interdictor with the kept SWD route can reflash at RDP-0. Only the user's mandatory pre-first-power verification catches that.
- No durable hardware key erase exists while the BHK is reloadable from flash; a tamper event depends on software running at the next boot.
- Until #50/#81 land, non-secure code can clear TAMP1E.
- Until #705 lands, a sealed unit's boot fingerprint is dark.
- Decap/FIB and silicon-vendor compromise stay out of scope (HARDENING.md:14).

skeptic.reason:
The core survives: a mechanical/PCB spec for the MP board (Tier A) plus an optional passive PC13 input (Tier B), with the active mesh dropped. I re-read the load-bearing code and docs and found nothing that sinks it, but two of its claims are wrong and several are overstated.

What I confirmed by reading:
- secure/src/hw/tamp.rs:272 writes TAMP_SCR = 0x0007_FFFF unconditionally at init. The only TAMP_SR reads are tamp.rs:86 (poll) and :372 (IRQ), and both test only ITAMP_FLAG_MASK. No TAMPxE bit is ever set.
- secure/src/hw/bhk.rs:27-33: the backup registers are regenerated from flash page 126 every boot, so hardware BKPR erase is not a durable response.
- secure/src/main.rs:1400 (tamp::init) precedes :1529 (bhk::load_and_lock); poll is called from SysTick near :4327.
- Makefile:2662 and :2718: RELEASE_FEATURES and PROD_SHIP_FEATURES carry tamp,tamp-wipe,tzic-wipe,bhk and no tamp-irq, so shipping is polled.
- secure/src/board/pq1.rs:345: FREE_PINS = PA10, PC13, PB4. Pin table PDF: pin 1 VBAT, pin 2 PC13 NC, HSE 8M on 3/4, LSE 32K on 5/6, PA0/PA1 are the keys.
- docs/hardware/pcb/README.md: six-layer stack, so stripline is physically possible.
- docs/security/user-device-verification.md:163-168 and :184-191, brownout-hardening.md:216-250, evt-debug-pins.md:144-176 say what the recommendation says they say. The VBAT and SWD-route conflicts are real.

skeptic.corrections:
1. WRONG CLAIM, and it changes Tier B. "A button tap leaks the PIN press pattern, not the seed" is false. secure/src/ui/seed_wizard.rs:3, :106, :130-166 has a "Restore" mode that enters all 24 words through the two buttons (PA0/PA1). The intrusion-wipe resume at main.rs:1938-1952 ends with show_status("WALLET WIPED", "restore from seed") and drops into that wizard.
   - Consequence: Tier B's response (trigger_intrusion_wipe) sends the owner to re-type the seed on a device that was just opened. A two-wire button tap then captures the whole mnemonic, with no SPI tap needed. An evil maid can open the case deliberately to cause this.
   - Fix (a): Tier B must end in a distinct, persistent "CASE OPENED — do not restore on this unit" state. It must not look like the PIN-lockout wipe screen, and it needs a deliberate acknowledgement. That is new durable state and new UI, not "tens of lines".
   - Fix (b): rank the button nets equal to SPI1/DC in Tier A. Buttons cannot be buried, so the dome-switch region needs the potting/no-void treatment too.
   - Fix (c): add this to residual_after. Restore on a previously-opened unit is seed-compromising regardless of the display.

2. OVERCLAIM: "copper rule (the only near-deterministic part)". Stripline protects only the middle of each net. Every display net still surfaces at the UFQFPN48 perimeter lands, the FPC connector pads, the FPC tail and the panel edge. The attacker's next step is a tap at one of those. No part of Tier A is deterministic; call all of it attacker-cost and evidence.
   - Add a prerequisite: read the L2-L5 copper plots to see whether V10 already routes SPI1/DC on inner layers. docs/hardware/pcb/README.md says no tamper review of the artwork has been done.

3. Missing recorded decision. README.md:449 already says "retain only the SWD + NRST verification pads required for pre-first-power inspection". That is a second recorded SWD route (internal pads), alongside user-device-verification.md:184-189 (SBU) and evt-debug-pins.md:161.
   - Tier A item 2 ("no test pads on S-world") must explicitly exempt SWD/NRST, or supersede README:449.
   - Internal pads plus a welded shell is exactly the incompatible combination. The owner decision must retire one of the three texts.
   - BOOT0 is also a pad today (J211/TP103, evt-debug-pins.md:144). Add it to the pad-removal list.

4. Live defect 1 (SCR clear before read): CONFIRMED by code, with scope and reachability corrected.
   - Narrower than stated. 0x0007_FFFF clears SR bits 0-18 only. ITAMP3 is LSE-CSS and inert under the LSI clocking at tamp.rs:225-262. So in today's build only ITAMP1 (backup-domain voltage) and ITAMP2 (temperature) are discarded. ITAMP5/6/8/9/11/12/13 survive to the first poll and still wipe, including ITAMP9, the crypto-fault canary. The phrase "voltage glitch" overstates it: ITAMP1 watches the backup-domain rail, not a core-VDD glitch.
   - More reachable than stated. An NRST pulse is a system reset, not a backup-domain reset, so flags persist whatever the VBAT wiring is. The "depends on VBAT wiring" hedge applies only to the power-removal variant. An attacker who drives NRST within about 1 ms of the stimulus wins every time in polled mode.
   - The same boot-time read-before-clear also covers an IRQ-mode wipe that is power-cut before arm_wipe_flag lands.
   - Severity: low-medium today. It becomes a hard blocker for Tier B, because TAMP1F is bit 0, inside the clear mask, and the "latched while unplugged" case depends on reading it at boot.
   - Fix shape: read SR at init, escalate if any enabled flag is set, then clear. The clear must still precede bhk::load_and_lock.
   - Not reproduced on silicon (#391).

5. Live defect 2 (external input inert): CONFIRMED (tamp.rs:274-281, :87, :372). Informational gap.

6. Live defect 3 (stale claims): CONFIRMED, and incomplete. Add:
   - tamp.rs:78-81 (poll doc: "NEVER halts, NEVER wipes") and :360-364 (on_tamp_irq doc: "Never halts and never wipes") are false under tamp-wipe.
   - tamp.rs:61-63 says polled mode leaves "IER stays masked", but init_tamp_registers writes TAMP_IER with the full mask unconditionally at about :308-322. Only the NVIC enable is skipped.
   - main.rs:1402-1405 logs "log-only" in a tamp-wipe build.
   - hardware_requirements.md:104 and :239 and README.md:448 say "four layers"; the board is six-layer.
   - Issue #75's first checkbox is already done at tamp.rs:108 and :388.

7. Tier B gaps not flagged:
   - (a) A loop that stays open re-latches TAMP1F every boot, giving an endless wipe loop. Define the terminal state.
   - (b) The loop must be closed and verified before the first field boot. Otherwise the rdp2-self-lock path wipes or bricks brand-new units. Sequence it against first_boot Phase A.
   - (c) With FLTCR precharge enabled (TAMPPUDIS=0) the internal pull-up is used. An external pull + RC must be sized against the 8-cycle precharge or it will false-trip.
   - (d) "Select LSE as RTCCLK" hits the guard at tamp.rs:250-256: RTCSEL is write-once per backup-domain reset, so already-booted units keep LSI. LSE also adds a glitchable crystal, and README §A "no glitchable clock to S-world" is undecided.

8. Priority split is right but should be stated as two items, not one P1. Tier A spec, schematic/copper cross-check and the SWD/VBAT owner decisions are P1 and hardware-only. Tier B is P3, and should stay unbuilt unless correction 1(a) is accepted. Keeping the PC13 net routed to an unpopulated footprint costs nothing at respin. The SCR read-before-clear fix belongs with #75 at P2.

9. Tracked issues: the list is correct and complete for what exists. Additions worth linking: #52 (enumerate the 11 internal tampers) and #36 (WRP on the BHK page). No issue covers enclosure, stripline, pad removal, PC13 or TAMP_SCR.

live_defect.reachable_in_production_config: Yes for the code path: tamp + tamp-wipe, polled, is the shipping set. An NRST pulse within about 1 ms of an ITAMP1/ITAMP2 event discards the flag whatever the VBAT wiring is, because NRST does not reset the backup domain. Only ITAMP1 (backup-domain voltage) and ITAMP2 (temperature) are lost; ITAMP3 is inert under LSI, and ITAMP5-13, including ITAMP9, sit outside the clear mask and still wipe at the first poll. The production image cannot be built today (S-2 fence).
